findings.text: Generic virtual machine statistics expose two counters covering remote translation lookaside buffer flush activity, one for flushes performed and one for flush requests issued. The descriptors use a generic virtual machine scope and counter semantics.

Generic virtual CPU statistics cover halt polling effectiveness and timing. They include success and attempt counts, invalid poll counts, wakeup counts, nanosecond totals for successful polls, failed polls and waiting, logarithmic time histograms for those three durations sized by the halt poll history count, and a boolean blocking indicator. A time histogram helper builds second-based power-of-ten distributions with nanosecond scaling.

Histogram helpers provide saturating counting into caller supplied arrays. One form selects a bucket by scaling the observed value with a bucket size, while the other selects logarithmically. In both cases an index beyond the end is clamped to the final bucket and exactly one bucket is incremented per observation. A convenience wrapper supplies the array length automatically for the linear case.

The memory management unit invalidation retry check reports that the caller must retry when an invalidation is currently in progress or when the observed invalidation sequence differs from the sequence captured earlier. Otherwise it reports that the caller may proceed. The check is designed to work without holding the main MMU lock on some platforms.

The retry check orders its two reads so the in-progress flag is observed before the sequence number, pairing with a write barrier on the invalidation completion path. This ensures the caller sees either the old in-progress indication or the fresh sequence. On one platform the check runs under a per-page lock for scalability and must not depend on the global MMU lock for ordering.
The maximum number of interrupt routing entries is four thousand ninety six.

Fallback interrupt routing and eventfd helpers indicate an unconfigured build. Routing setup succeeds trivially and teardown does nothing. Eventfd signalling fails as invalid, release does nothing, and resampler notification reports no resampling performed.
Architecture fallback hooks provide permissive defaults. The poll suppression query always allows polling and the virtual CPU run pid change hook always reports success.
The virtual machine device holder links an operations table, the owning virtual machine, an opaque driver private area, and a list node chaining the device into the virtual machine device list.

The device operations table carries a name plus lifecycle handlers for creation, deferred initialization, destruction and file close release, attribute accessors for set, get and presence queries, and file handlers for control and mapping operations.

Device lifecycle entry points are creation, deferred initialization after successful creation, destruction which frees the device, release on file close which detaches the device, attribute handlers, and control and mapping handlers. Destruction timing relative to emulated input output teardown varies with outstanding references.
Creation and file close release run while holding the virtual machine lock, so work unsuitable under that lock must be deferred. Deferred initialization runs after creation without holding the lock.

A device moves from creation to deferred initialization on success, then remains attached until either destruction or file close release. Release removes the device from the virtual machine list and suppresses any later destruction call. Destruction may occur before or after emulated input output teardown depending on lingering references.
The dirty ring reserves sixty four entries and allows at most sixty five thousand five hundred thirty six entries.

The default guest memory page lookup unconditionally signals a bug against the virtual machine and reports an input output failure, indicating that real support must be provided elsewhere and that this fallback must never succeed.

A guest memory population callback type receives the virtual machine, a guest frame number and a host frame number, returning a status code. The routed fragment truncates the signature, so further parameters and the full contract are not visible here.

The resampler holder keeps the virtual machine, a list of sharing eventfds, an acknowledgement notifier, and a link chaining resamplers for the same global interrupt. The kernel eventfd holder keeps the virtual machine, wait queue linkage, a routing entry with sequence protection, a global interrupt number, injection and shutdown work items, resampler linkage with a resample eventfd, setup eventfd and list linkage, bypass consumer and producer linkage, and bypass virtual CPU association with data.

Resampler sharing lists use read copy update discipline with updates serialized by the resampler lock. The fast path routing entry is updated under the eventfd lock with sequence count protection for readers.
Paravirtual feature and hint queries test a single bit selected by the caller against an architecture supplied mask, reporting present when the corresponding bit is set.

Conditional export helpers control visibility of symbols to the core module and its submodules. One configuration exports to the core plus submodules, another exports only within submodules, and fallback configurations expand to nothing, disabling the export.

Guest virtual addresses and host virtual addresses use native word width, while guest physical addresses, guest frame numbers, host physical addresses, host frame numbers and the kernel page frame alias use sixty four bit width. The kernel page frame type aliases the host frame type.
The invalid guest physical address is the all bits set value. Halt poll histograms hold thirty two buckets. Statistic names allow forty eight bytes.

The guest frame to host virtual cache holds a generation, guest address, host address, length and memory slot. The guest frame to host frame cache adds the owning virtual machine, list linkage, a read write lock with a separate refresh mutex, a kernel virtual address, a page frame number, and active and valid flags.

The memory management unit memory cache describes a freelist pool with zeroing and custom allocation flags, an initialization value, a slab cache pointer, a capacity, a current object count, and an object pointer array.

Generic virtual machine counters hold remote flush and flush request totals. Generic virtual CPU counters hold halt poll success and attempt totals, invalid poll and wakeup totals, nanosecond totals for success, failure and wait, three thirty two entry histograms for those durations, and a blocking count.

Tracing uses a dedicated subsystem name and maps each exit reason code to a matching symbolic label covering faults, input output, hypercalls, debug, halts, interrupts, timers, and architecture specific exits. Interrupt chip identifiers map to labels distinguishing two programmable controller roles and the input output advanced controller.

Acknowledgement trace formatting has two conditional variants sharing pin information. One renders the chip identifier symbolically while the other renders it numerically, selected by build configuration.
Memory mapped input output trace kinds are unsatisfied read at zero, read at one, and write at two, each with a matching textual label.
Floating point unit tracing distinguishes unload at zero from load at one with corresponding labels.
The userspace interface version is twelve. Guest debugging support is advertised as present.

The basic memory region descriptor carries slot, flags, guest address, size and userspace address. The extended form adds a guest memory file offset, a file descriptor, padding, and reserved space for future growth.
Memory slot flags occupy low bits with dirty logging at bit zero, read only at bit one, and guest memory file backing at bit two.

The interrupt level descriptor carries either an interrupt number or a status value plus a level. The chip descriptor carries an identifier, padding, and a fixed size reservation that may overlay platform interrupt controller states.

The timer configuration holds flags with padding. The hypervisor exit descriptor discriminates synthetic interrupt, hypercall and debug variants with control and page or parameter fields. The Xen exit descriptor carries a hypercall with mode, privilege, input, result and parameters. The secure nested paging certificate request holds a guest address, page count and return code.

Timer speaker dummy equals one. Hypervisor synthetic interrupt equals one, hypercall equals two, debug equals three. Xen hypercall equals one. Secure key retrieval none equals one and the maximum key count equals one million forty eight thousand five hundred seventy six.

Early exit identifiers are unknown zero, exception one, input output two, hypercall three, debug four, halt five, memory mapped input output six, interrupt window open seven, shutdown eight, fail entry nine, interrupt ten, and set task priority register eleven.

Middle exit identifiers are task priority access twelve, s390 interception thirteen, s390 reset fourteen, device control fifteen and deprecated, non maskable interrupt sixteen, internal error seventeen, operating system interface eighteen, papr hypercall nineteen, s390 user control twenty, watchdog twenty one, and s390 channel twenty two.

Later exit identifiers are embedded performance twenty three, system event twenty four, s390 status twenty five, input output advanced controller end of interrupt twenty six, hyperv twenty seven, arm non secure interrupt twenty eight, x86 read model specific register twenty nine, x86 write model specific register thirty, dirty ring full thirty one, access point reset hold thirty two, and x86 bus lock thirty three.

Recent exit identifiers are Xen thirty four, riscv supervisor binary interface thirty five, riscv control register thirty six, notify thirty seven, loongarch input output control thirty eight, memory fault thirty nine, trust domain extensions forty, arm synchronous external abort forty one, arm sixty four byte load store forty two, and secure nested paging certificate request forty three.
Internal error subtypes are emulation one, simultaneous exception two, delivery event three, and unexpected exit reason four. The emulation instruction bytes flag occupies bit zero.
An unsafe hint marker has two build variants. One decorates the given symbol to denote unsafe use inside the hypervisor, while the other leaves the symbol unchanged.

The run descriptor starts with interrupt window and immediate exit requests, an exit reason with interrupt injection readiness and flag state, control registers, and on one architecture a processor status word. A discriminated union then overlays per exit payloads for hardware, fail entry, exception, input output, debug, memory mapped input output, hypercall, task priority, s390, device control, internal error with an emulation failure overlay preserving backward compatibility, operating system interface, papr, channel, external performance, and the start of system events.

Input output directions are input zero and output one. The visible system event types are shutdown one and reset two. Further system event types and later run union members lie beyond the routed truncation and are not claimed here.
Header guards mark inclusion protection for the eventfd, paravirtual, type, trace and userspace interface headers.

Device destruction and file close release are mutually exclusive. Once release detaches the device, destruction must not run. Callers must tolerate destruction occurring on either side of emulated input output teardown.
